Stake history sysvar read, init, update, and account encoding logic.

# Purpose
`fd_sysvar_stake_history.c` implements read and write support for the `stake_history` sysvar account. It uses the sysvar account ID, the transaction account helpers, and the bank/account database interfaces to store and load a `fd_stake_history_t` value in bincode form. The [`write_stake_history`](<#write_stake_history>) helper encodes the in-memory stake history into a fixed-size aligned buffer and updates the sysvar account through `fd_sysvar_account_update`. The [`fd_sysvar_stake_history_read`](<#fd_sysvar_stake_history_read>) function reads the account from `funk`, rejects missing accounts and zero-lamport accounts, and decodes the account data into a caller-supplied `fd_stake_history_t`.

The file also defines sysvar lifecycle functions. [`fd_sysvar_stake_history_init`](<#fd_sysvar_stake_history_init>) creates a new empty stake history with `fd_stake_history_new` and writes it to the sysvar account. [`fd_sysvar_stake_history_update`](<#fd_sysvar_stake_history_update>) reads the current history, updates the ring-buffer position, stores the new epoch entry values from `fd_epoch_stake_history_entry_pair_t`, and writes the updated state back. This code is part of the sysvar management layer and provides the external interface used to maintain stake history state in the bank.
